newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian Commercial Bank net profit up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Romanian Commercial Bank net profit up in 1996.

text.p: Romania's state-owned Banca Comerciala Romana SA (BCR) said on Friday 1996 net profit rose to 557.2 billion lei from 484.32 billion in 1995.
"The profit tax was lower as the bank paid larger taxation the previous year (1995)," BCR marketing manager Marian Busca said.
He said gross profit diminished to 613.67 billion lei last year from 686.97 billion in 1995 as the bank had higher spending on expanding its network across Romania.
The bank's total assets rose to 8.76 trillion lei from 4.73 trillion at end-1995. It decided to pay 172.97 billion lei total dividends, up from 144.87 billion in 1995.
All figures were reported in nominal terms. Inflation was 56.9 percent last year, up from 27.8 percent in 1995.
BCR, which specialised in industry financing before the 1989 fall of communism, continues to manage the bulk of loans granted to industrial companies.
The bank's capital rose to 216.74 billion lei in 1996 from 109.1 billion at end-1995 after including some fixed assets as capital contribution, Busca said.
The State Ownership Fund holds 70 percent of its share capital, with regional private ownership funds taking the rest.

The centrist government, which ousted ex-Communists in last year's elections, has pledged to privatise the country's six state-run banks under an ambitious market reform programme. A bank selloff bill is to be discussed by parliament next week.
The BCR is seen as too large for early privatisation. The government said the first bank fit for privatisation was development bank Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare SA. ($=7,053 lei)
